posts.content:
Indoor rock climbing is a popular and exciting sport that requires a combination of strength, endurance, and technique. One of the most important aspects of this sport is the equipment, and having the right gear can make a huge difference in your climbing experience.

 In this blog post, we will discuss the different types of indoor rock climbing equipment and what you should consider when purchasing them. First and foremost, it is important to have a good pair of climbing shoes. These shoes should fit snugly and provide adequate support and grip. They should also be comfortable, as climbing can be an intense activity and you don't want to be dealing with blisters or sore feet halfway through your climb.

Look for shoes with rubber soles and a snug fit around the heel to ensure a good grip on the climbing wall. Additionally, you'll want to choose a climbing shoe with the correct level of stiffness. More stiff shoes will be better for edging and small hold climbing. Softer shoes will be better for smearing and slab climbing.

Next, you will need a harness to secure yourself to the climbing wall. A harness is designed to hold your weight in the event of a fall and it is one of the most important pieces of equipment you will need. Look for a harness with adjustable leg loops and a comfortable waistbelt, you also want to ensure that it is safe, durable and easy to use. There are different types of harnesses available: -traditional (waist and leg loops) -sport climbing specific (single tie-in point, often has gear loops) -big wall/aid climbing specific (multiple tie-in points, gear loops and hauling attachments)

Another important piece of equipment is a belay device. This device attaches to the harness and is used to control the rope and keep the climber safe while they are climbing. There are many different types of belay devices available, but the most popular ones are the Black Diamond ATC, Petzl GriGri, and Mammut Smart. These devices are easy to use, reliable, and provide good braking power.

You'll also want to consider the rope, which is what keeps you secure while climbing. There are two main types of rope: dynamic and static. Dynamic ropes are elastic and are designed to stretch a little when a fall occurs, which helps to reduce the shock on the climber's body. Static ropes, on the other hand, do not stretch, and are primarily used for hauling gear or for rappelling. Look for a rope that is thick, strong and durable to ensure your safety. Dynamic rope are the most common types used for climbing and a good rule of thumb is to look for ropes with a diameter of 10-11mm and have a minimum impact force of 8kN

Finally, you will need a set of carabiners and quickdraws. Carabiners are metal loops with a spring-loaded gate that can be used to connect the rope to anchors, while quickdraws are used to connect the rope to the climbing wall. There are different types of carabiners and quickdraws available, but the most popular ones are the Black Diamond Positron and the Petzl Spirit. Look for carabiners and quickdraws that are lightweight, durable and easy to use.

FAQ

What types of equipment do I need for rock climbing at a gym?

The most essential equipment for rock climbing at a gym includes climbing shoes, a chalk bag, and a harness. Climbing shoes are specially designed to provide the necessary grip and support for climbing. A chalk bag is used to keep your hands dry and provide a better grip on the holds. A harness is used to attach you to the rope while climbing. Other equipment that you may need includes a belay device, carabiners, and a helmet.

What is the difference between a lead climbing and top-rope climbing?

Lead climbing and top-rope climbing are two different types of climbing that use different techniques and equipment. Lead climbing involves the climber attaching the rope to quickdraws as they climb, and the belayer pays out slack as the climber ascends. Top-rope climbing involves the rope being anchored to the top of the route and the belayer holds the rope tight as the climber ascends. Lead climbing is considered more challenging and requires more skill and experience, while top-rope climbing is more beginner-friendly.

What is the difference between a belay device and a carabiner?

A belay device is a piece of equipment used to control the rope while belaying, or supporting, a climber. A carabiner, on the other hand, is a metal loop with a spring-loaded gate that is used to connect the rope to the harness, anchor, or other climbing gear. A belay device attaches to the harness of the belayer, while carabiners attach to the harness of the climber and the anchors on the wall.

How do I choose the right climbing shoes for gym climbing?

When choosing climbing shoes for gym climbing, it's important to consider the type of climbing you'll be doing, your skill level, and the fit of the shoe. For gym climbing, you'll typically want a shoe that is designed for sport climbing or indoor climbing. These shoes typically have a flat profile, a stiff sole, and a tight fit to provide maximum control and precision on the holds. It's also important to try on different brands and sizes to ensure a proper fit.

First, let's talk about traditional climbing shoes. These shoes are designed for traditional climbing, also known as trad climbing, which involves placing and removing gear as you climb. They typically have a more relaxed fit and a downturned toe, which allows for better edging and smearing on small holds. The La Sportiva Mythos and the Five Ten Anasazi are both great options for traditional climbing shoes, as they offer a comfortable fit and excellent performance on small holds.

Next, we have sport climbing shoes. These shoes are designed for sport climbing, which involves pre-placed bolts on the rock face. They typically have a tighter fit and a more aggressive downturned toe, which allows for maximum power and precision on steep routes. The Scarpa Instinct VS and the Black Diamond Momentum are both top contenders for sport climbing shoes, as they offer a snug fit and outstanding performance on overhanging routes.

Finally, we have bouldering shoes. Bouldering shoes are designed for bouldering, which is a form of climbing that takes place on short, difficult routes without the use of ropes. They typically have a very tight fit and a flat or slightly downturned toe, which allows for maximum sensitivity and control on small holds. The Butora Acro and the Evolv Shaman are both excellent choices for bouldering shoes, as they offer a snug fit and unbeatable performance on technical boulder problems.

It's important to note that everyone's feet are different and what works for one person may not work for another. So, when purchasing climbing shoes, it's important to try on multiple pairs and consider factors such as fit, comfort, and performance.

FAQ

What are the best climbing shoes for intermediate climbers?

Intermediate climbers typically look for shoes that offer a moderate to aggressive downturn and a moderate to high level of stiffness. These shoes will help with precision and power during more challenging routes. Some popular options for intermediate climbers include the Scarpa Instinct VS and the Black Diamond Momentum.

What are the best climbing shoes for beginners?

For beginners, it's best to look for climbing shoes with a flat or slightly downturned shape and a neutral to moderate stiffness. These shoes will provide a good balance of support and comfort while you're still learning the basics. Some popular options for beginners include the La Sportiva Mythos and the Five Ten Anasazi VCS.

How do I know if my climbing shoes fit properly?

A proper fit is crucial for climbing shoes as they should fit snugly but not be too tight. Your toes should be able to wiggle slightly but not move around too much. When trying on shoes, make sure to wear the socks you plan to climb in and make sure the shoes are laced tightly.

What are the best climbing shoes for advanced climbers?

Advanced climbers often look for shoes with an aggressive downturn and a high level of stiffness. These shoes are designed for maximum precision and power on the most challenging routes. Some popular options for advanced climbers include the La Sportiva Solution and the Five Ten Blackwing.

How do I take care of my climbing shoes?

To take care of your climbing shoes, make sure to clean them after each climb to remove dirt and debris. You can use a soft brush and mild soap to clean the shoes. Avoid exposing your shoes to direct sunlight or heat, as this can cause the shoes to dry out and become brittle. And it's better to store them in a cool and dry place. Also, you can apply a leather conditioner to keep the leather supple.

Climbing is an exhilarating and challenging sport that requires a great deal of skill, strength, and endurance. One of the most important pieces of equipment for any climber is the harness. First, let's take a look at the different types of climbing harnesses available. The most common types are the traditional waist harness, the sit harness, and the full-body harness. The traditional waist harness is the most basic type and is worn around the waist, providing support for your lower back and hips. The sit harness, also known as a seat harness, is worn around the hips and legs and is ideal for climbers who spend a lot of time hanging or resting in their harness. The full-body harness is the most comprehensive type of harness and covers the entire body, providing support for the back, chest, and legs.

Another important factor to consider when choosing a climbing harness is safety. Additionally, look for a harness that has a belay loop, which is the attachment point for the belay device, and a tie-in point, which is the attachment point for the rope. These points should be reinforced and made of durable materials to ensure that they can withstand the stresses of climbing.

Types of Climbing Harness

A climbing harness is an essential piece of equipment for rock climbers, providing a secure attachment point for the rope and protection in the event of a fall. There are several types of climbing harnesses, each designed for a specific type of climbing. Here are the most common types:

Sport Climbing Harness

These harnesses are designed for use in sport climbing, which involves climbing routes with pre-installed bolts for protection. They are typically lightweight and have minimal padding to allow for maximum freedom of movement.

Trad Climbing Harness

Trad climbing, short for "traditional" climbing, involves placing gear, such as nuts and cams, in cracks and other features in the rock for protection. Trad climbing harnesses tend to have more padding and a higher tie-in point for comfort during long climbs.

Big Wall Climbing Harness

Big wall climbing involves multi-day ascents of large rock faces, and requires a harness with additional features, such as gear loops, haul loops, and comfortable padding for extended periods of hanging.

Mountaineering Harness

Designed for use in alpine environments, mountaineering harnesses have adjustable leg loops to accommodate bulky clothing, and may have additional features for use with ice axes and crampons.

Gym Climbing Harness

Gym climbing harnesses are designed specifically for use in indoor climbing gyms. They tend to have minimal padding and are often adjustable to fit a wide range of body types.

When selecting a climbing harness, it is important to choose one that is appropriate for the type of climbing you will be doing. A harness that is comfortable and fits well can make a big difference in your climbing experience, so it is worth investing in a high-quality harness that meets your specific needs.

FAQ

How many gear loops should a climbing harness have?

 The number of gear loops on a climbing harness can vary, but most climbing harnesses have 4 gear loops. This provides ample space for climbing gear and tools and are positioned in a way that allows for easy access to your gear while climbing.

What are the best materials for a climbing harness?

The best materials for a climbing harness are high-strength, abrasion-resistant webbing and durable aluminum buckles. These materials ensure the harness can withstand the rigors of climbing and will last through multiple climbing adventures.

Should I choose a harness based on color?

While color can be a personal preference, it should not be the primary factor in choosing a climbing harness. Factors such as materials, durability, gear loops, and fit are more important in determining the best harness for your needs.

Are adjustable leg loops important in a climbing harness?

Yes, adjustable leg loops are important in a climbing harness as they allow for a customized fit and to accommodate different layers of clothing. This ensures that the harness is comfortable for the user and allows for optimal movement.

What is the best type of waistbelt for a climbing harness?

posts.content:
Rock climbing ropes are one of the most essential pieces of equipment for any rock climber. They provide the safety and security needed to ascend and descend the rock face, and choosing the right type of climbing rope can make a huge difference in your climbing experience. This blog will expose you to the best climbing gear, from durable rope, bi-pattern rope,  workhorse rope, multi-pitch climbing ropes, gym climbing rope and also discuss various climbing rope features like the rope length, rope diameter and reviews on selection of the best climbing rope for your needs.

In this article, we will explore the top rated climbing ropes for rock climbers and the features that make them stand out. First, let’s talk about the two main types of climbing ropes: dynamic and static. Dynamic ropes are designed to stretch under load, which helps to absorb the energy of a fall and reduce the force on the climber. They are best for lead climbing, where the rope is used to catch a fall. Static ropes, on the other hand, are designed to not stretch under load, and are best for rappelling, hauling, and other non-fall applications.

When it comes to dynamic ropes, the Beal Joker 9.1mm is a favorite among rock climbers. This rope is incredibly durable, with a high impact force rating of 8.6 kN, making it perfect for lead climbing. It also has a low impact force rating of 5.2 kN, making it great for top-roping. The Beal Joker 9.1mm is a great all-around rope that can be used for a variety of climbing styles.

Another great option for dynamic ropes is the Edelrid MegaJul. This rope has a diameter of 7.8mm, making it one of the thinnest and lightest ropes on the market. It also has a high impact force rating of 8.1 kN, making it perfect for lead climbing. Its low impact force rating of 5.1 kN, makes it also great for top-roping. The Edelrid MegaJul is a great choice for climbers who want a lightweight rope that can handle a lot of wear and tear.

For static ropes, the Mammut Infinity Protect 9.5mm is a top pick. This rope has a high breaking strength of 22 kN, making it perfect for rappelling and hauling. It also has a low stretch of 1.4%, making it perfect for applications where minimal stretch is needed. The Mammut Infinity Protect 9.5mm is a great choice for climbers who need a strong and reliable rope for rappelling and hauling.

Another great option for static ropes is the Sterling Evolution Velocity 9.8mm. This rope has a high breaking strength of 24 kN, making it perfect for heavy loads. It also has a low stretch of 2.3%, making it perfect for applications where minimal stretch is needed. The Sterling Evolution Velocity 9.8mm is a great choice for climbers who need a strong and reliable rope for heavy loads.

When choosing a climbing rope, it is important to consider the type of climbing you will be doing, as well as the rope’s diameter, impact force rating, and stretch. You should also consider the rope’s durability, as it will be exposed to a lot of wear and tear. Additionally, it’s important to consider your personal preference, as it is important to feel comfortable with the rope you choose.

Types of Ropes

Climbing ropes are an essential piece of equipment for climbers of all levels. They come in different sizes, lengths, and materials, making it essential to choose the right one for your specific needs. In this article, we’ll discuss the best climbing ropes available on the market and what makes them stand out.

Sterling Evolution Velocity

The Sterling Evolution Velocity is a popular choice for climbers due to its excellent balance of weight, durability, and handling. This rope is available in different lengths and diameters, making it suitable for various climbing activities, from sport climbing to big wall climbing. The Sterling Evolution Velocity is also easy to handle, which is essential for climbers who need to make quick and precise movements.

Mammut Infinity Dry

The Mammut Infinity Dry is a top-of-the-line rope that provides excellent durability and handling. The rope is treated with a dry coating that makes it resistant to water, dirt, and abrasion, which is crucial for climbers who often climb in wet or dirty conditions. The Mammut Infinity Dry is also lightweight, making it easy to carry and use during long climbing trips.

The rope is available in different lengths and diameters, making it easy to choose the right one for your specific needs. The Petzl Volta also has a dry treatment that makes it resistant to water, dirt, and abrasion, which is essential for climbers who often climb in wet or dirty conditions.

Black Diamond 9.9mm

The Black Diamond 9.9mm is a popular rope among climbers due to its excellent balance of durability, handling, and price. The rope is available in different lengths and is suitable for various climbing activities, from ice climbing to big wall climbing. The Black Diamond 9.9mm is also easy to handle, making it an excellent choice for climbers who need to make quick and precise movements.

Edelweiss Curve 9.8mm

The Edelweiss Curve 9.8mm is a lightweight and versatile rope that is suitable for a wide range of climbing activities. The rope is treated with a dry coating that makes it resistant to water, dirt, and abrasion, which is crucial for climbers who often climb in wet or dirty conditions. The Edelweiss Curve 9.8mm also has excellent handling, which is essential for climbers who need to make quick and precise movements.

In conclusion, the best climbing rope for you will depend on your specific needs and preferences. However, the ropes listed above are all excellent options that provide excellent durability, handling, and versatility. Before choosing a rope, make sure to consider the type of climbing you’ll be doing, the length and diameter you’ll need, and any specific features, such as dry treatments, that may be necessary for your climbing conditions.

How Do I Choose A Climbing Rope?

When choosing a climbing rope that suites your specific need, there are some questions that comes to mind about how to make the right choice and get the best value for your money. Below are some questiosn you might want to ask yourself before making a selection.

1. Do you need a durable rope or a better handling rope?

When it comes to choosing a climbing rope, one of the biggest decisions you'll have to make is whether you prioritize durability or handling. A durable rope will be able to withstand more wear and tear, while a rope with better handling will be easier to use and manipulate.

If you're primarily climbing indoors, a rope with better handling might be more important, since you won't have to worry as much about the rope getting damaged by rocks or rough terrain. On the other hand, if you're planning to do a lot of outdoor climbing, a more durable rope might be a better investment.

When choosing a rope, consider the  climbing type you'll be doing, your personal preferences, and your budget. You might also want to ask for recommendations from experienced climbers or do some research online to find the best options.

2. How Do I Choose A Climbing Rope?

Choosing a climbing rope can be a daunting task, but there are a few key factors to consider that can help simplify the process. Here are some things to keep in mind:

  • Length: Consider the climbs you'll be doing and choose a rope that's long enough to accommodate them. A longer rope will give you more options, but might be heavier and harder to handle.

  • Diameter: The diameter of a rope will affect its weight, handling, and durability. Thicker ropes are generally more durable, while thinner ropes are easier to handle.

  • Material: Climbing ropes are typically made of either nylon or polyester. Nylon is more stretchy and durable, while polyester is more static and lightweight.

  • UIAA Certification: Look for ropes that are certified by the Union Internationale des Associations d'Alpinisme (UIAA) to ensure they meet safety standards.

  • Personal Preferences: Ultimately, the best rope for you will depend on your personal preferences, as well as the climbs you'll be doing.

By considering these factors and doing some research, you can find the perfect rope for your needs.

3. What Rope Length Should You Get for the Gym?

When choosing a rope for indoor climbing, you'll generally want to go with a shorter length than you would for outdoor climbing. A 60-meter rope is usually sufficient for most gym climbs, but you can also go shorter if you prefer.

Shorter ropes are generally easier to handle and less cumbersome, which can be an advantage in the gym. However, a longer rope will give you more options for climbing routes and can be useful for practicing longer climbs.

Ultimately, the length of rope you choose will depend on your personal preferences and the climbs you'll be doing.

4. What Diameter for Gym Climbing Ropes?

The diameter of a gym rope will affect its weight, handling, and durability. Thicker ropes are generally more durable but can be heavier and harder to handle. Thinner ropes are easier to handle but might not be as durable.

For indoor climbing, a diameter of around 9.5-10mm is generally a good choice. This size strikes a good balance between weight, handling, and durability.

However, as with length, the diameter of a rope is ultimately a matter of personal preference, so you should try out different sizes to find the one that works best for you.

5. Can You Also Use Gym Climbing Ropes for Outdoor Climbing?

While gym ropes can technically be used for outdoor climbing, it's generally not recommended. Gym ropes are usually shorter and thinner than outdoor ropes, which can make them less safe and less durable for outdoor climbing.

In addition, outdoor climbing often involves rougher terrain, which can damage gym ropes more easily. Outdoor ropes are also usually certified for outdoor use, meaning they meet certain safety standards and are more reliable in outdoor conditions.

If you're planning to do a lot of outdoor climbing, it's generally best to invest in a dedicated outdoor climbing rope. However, if you're just getting started or only plan to do occasional outdoor climbs, a gym rope can work in a pinch.

6. Best Overall Rock Climbing Rope

When it comes to the best overall rock climbing rope, there are a few key factors to consider, including durability, handling, and weight. One top pick is the Petzl Volta 9.2mm rope, which offers a great balance of handling and durability. It's also lightweight, making it a great choice for longer climbs.

Another excellent option is the Sterling Evolution Velocity 9.8mm rope, which is durable and easy to handle. It also has a middle marker to help you keep track of your rope length. Ultimately, the best rope for you will depend on your personal preferences and the climbs types you'll be doing, so be sure to do your research and read reviews before making a purchase.

7. Best for Alpine and Multi-Pitch Climbing

When it comes to alpine and multi-pitch climbing, you'll want a rope that's both durable and lightweight. One top pick is the Mammut Infinity Dry 9.5mm rope, which is both strong and lightweight. It also has a dry treatment, making it resistant to water and dirt.

Another great option is the Beal Joker 9.1mm rope, which is super lightweight and easy to handle. It also has a Unicore construction, which helps prevent sheath slippage and makes it more durable. Ultimately, the best rope for alpine and multi-pitch climbing will depend on your personal preferences and the climbs you'll be doing. Be sure to do your research and consider factors like weight, durability, and handling before making a purchase.

With the right rope, you'll be able to climb with confidence and safety.

FAQ

What is the difference between a dynamic and a static rope?

Dynamic ropes are designed to stretch under load, which helps to absorb the impact of a fall. This makes them the best option for climbing as they reduce the impact force on the climber and anchors. Static ropes, on the other hand, do not stretch and are mainly used in rescue and industrial applications where a rope needs to be fixed in place.

What is the difference between a single and a half rope?

Single ropes are designed to be used alone, while half ropes are designed to be used in pairs. When using half ropes, the climber clips into both ropes, which provides increased security and reduces the risk of rope drag. This makes them a popular choice for trad climbing, where the route may have multiple pitches.

How often should I replace my climbing rope?

The lifespan of a climbing rope is determined by several factors such as the number of falls, the type of use, and the level of maintenance. Generally, a rope should be retired after it has been used for a significant number of falls, has visible damage, or after five years of use, whichever comes first.

What is the best type of rope for climbing?

The best type of rope for climbing depends on the type of climbing you will be doing. For sport climbing, a thinner rope with a diameter of around 9.8mm or less is ideal. For trad climbing, a thicker rope with a diameter of around 10.2mm or more is recommended for added durability. It is also important to consider the rope's strength, handling, and safety features.

The first thing to consider when choosing a climbing carabiner is the type of climbing you will be doing. There are several different types of carabiners available, each designed for specific types of climbing:

  • Straight-gate carabiners: These are the most basic and versatile type of carabiners. They are suitable for all types of climbing and are commonly used to connect the rope to anchors, belay devices, and other gear.

  • Bent-gate carabiners: These carabiners have a bent gate, which makes them easier to clip into bolts, anchors, and other fixed gear. They are commonly used for sport climbing, trad climbing, and alpine climbing.

  • Locking carabiners: These carabiners have a mechanism that locks the gate in place, preventing it from accidentally opening. They are commonly used for belaying, rappelling, and other safety-critical applications.

  • Key-locking carabiners: These carabiners have a key-locking mechanism that prevents the gate from snagging on gear or clothing. They are commonly used for sport climbing, trad climbing, and alpine climbing.

The next thing to consider when choosing a climbing carabiner is the size and weight of the carabiner. Larger carabiners are stronger and can hold more weight, but they are also heavier. Smaller carabiners are lighter and more compact, but they are not as strong. It’s important to choose a carabiner that is suitable for the type of climbing you will be doing and that meets your personal preferences.

When it comes to using climbing carabiners, it’s important to follow proper techniques to ensure your safety. Always make sure the carabiner is properly attached to the anchor, belay device, or other climbing gear. Avoid twisting or cross-loading the carabiner, as this can weaken the connection and increase the risk of failure. When clipping into bolts or anchors, be sure to use the correct clipping technique to ensure the carabiner is properly oriented and the gate is facing the right direction.

Proper maintenance is also essential for ensuring the longevity and safety of your climbing carabiners. Always inspect your carabiners before each use, looking for signs of wear, damage, or corrosion. Clean them regularly to remove dirt, debris, and other contaminants that can weaken the connection.

Types of Carabiners for Rock Climbing

Carabiners are an essential piece of equipment in climbing, used for attaching ropes, slings, and other equipment to a harness or anchor. In this article, we’ll explore the most common types of climbing carabiners and what makes them best suited for different climbing situations.

Non-locking Carabiners

Non-locking carabiners are the most commonly used carabiners in climbing. They come in various shapes and sizes, including the classic oval shape, D-shape, and asymmetrical shape. Non-locking carabiners are easy to use, lightweight, and cost-effective. They are ideal for situations where quick and frequent clipping and unclipping is required, such as during lead climbing or when building anchors.

Screw lock Carabiners

Screw lock carabiners have a threaded sleeve that can be screwed open or closed to lock the gate in place. This feature provides an extra layer of safety, making screw lock carabiners ideal for situations where security is a top priority. Screw lock carabiners are commonly used for belaying, rappelling, and setting up anchors.

Auto-locking Carabiners

Auto-locking carabiners have a spring-loaded mechanism that automatically locks the gate when it’s closed. They are easy to use and provide added security, making them ideal for situations where safety is a top priority, such as when belaying or rappelling. Auto locking carabiners are available in various shapes and sizes, including the D-shape and asymmetrical shape.

Best Belay Carabiner

Belay carabiners are designed specifically for use with belay devices. They have a pear or oval shape, which helps prevent the belay device from shifting or rotating, reducing the risk of accidental release. Belay carabiners are often larger than other carabiners, providing ample space for the rope and belay device to move freely.

Wiregate Carabiners

Wiregate carabiners are lighter and easier to handle than traditional solid gate carabiners. They are ideal for situations where weight and speed are a top priority, such as when climbing long routes. Wiregate carabiners are less likely to freeze shut in cold temperatures, making them a popular choice for ice climbing and winter mountaineering.

In conclusion, choosing the right carabiner depends on the type of climbing you’re doing and the situation you’re in. Whether you’re lead climbing, belaying, or setting up an anchor, there’s a carabiner that’s best suited for your needs. FAQ

How do I choose the right size of carabiner for my needs?

The size of a carabiner is determined by its gate opening, which is the distance between the gate and the spine. A larger gate opening allows for easier clipping and unclipping of ropes and gear, while a smaller gate opening is more secure. The size of the carabiner should be chosen based on the type of climbing and the size of the gear being used.

Can I use a carabiner multiple times or is it a one-time use item?

Carabiners can be used multiple times as long as they are in good condition and have not been subjected to any extreme forces. However, it is important to inspect your carabiners regularly for any signs of wear or damage, and to replace them if necessary.

What material are climbing carabiners made of?

Climbing carabiners are typically made of aluminum alloy. They are lightweight, durable and resist to corrosion.

What is the strength rating of a climbing carabiner?

The strength rating of a climbing carabiner is measured in kilonewtons (kN). It is the amount of force that a carabiner can withstand before breaking. A carabiner rated for 20kN is considered safe for most climbing activities.

What are the different types of climbing carabiners?

There are several types of climbing carabiners, including keylock, twistlock, and traditional gate carabiners. Keylock carabiners have a smooth, key-shaped nose that prevents snagging on gear and ropes, while twistlock carabiners have a locking mechanism that twists to close. Traditional gate carabiners have a simple gate that opens and closes.

A climbing helmet is designed to protect the head from falling debris, impact, and penetration. In this blog post, we will discuss the importance of wearing a helmet while climbing, the different types of helmets available, from the best lightweight climbing helmet on the market and how to choose the right helmet for your needs.

Climbing is a thrilling and exhilarating sport, but it also comes with its own set of risks. One of the most important pieces of gear that a climber can have is a helmet A climbing helmet is a type of head protection worn by rock climbers, mountaineers, and other individuals who engage in vertical activities such as caving and canyoneering. Climbing helmets are designed to protect the head from impacts and other types of injuries that can occur while climbing, particularly from falling rocks, ice, or other debris.

Most climbing helmets consist of a hard outer shell made of plastic or composite materials that absorb impacts and distribute the force over a larger area. The inner shell is made of foam or other materials that provide additional impact protection and cushioning for the head. Many climbing helmets also have an adjustable suspension system that allows the user to customize the fit and make the helmet more comfortable to wear.

READ: 8 Best Upper Limits Indoor Rock Climbing Gym Equipment: Top Rated Climbing Gears in 2023

 

Why You Should Always Wear a Helmet While Climbing

Climbing is a dangerous sport, and accidents can happen at any time. One of the most common types of accidents is a fall, which can result in serious head injuries. A helmet is designed to protect the head from impact, penetration, and falling debris. It is the first line of defense against injury and can mean the difference between life and death.

Wearing a helmet while climbing is not just a good idea, it is a must. In fact, many climbing gyms and outdoor climbing areas require climbers to wear helmets while climbing. This is because they understand the importance of head protection and want to ensure the safety of their climbers.

Types of Climbing Helmets

There are two main types of climbing helmets: hardshell and foam helmets. Hardshell helmets are made of a hard plastic shell that is designed to protect the head from impact. They are also lightweight and durable, making them a popular choice for climbers. Foam helmets, on the other hand, are made of a lightweight foam material that is designed to absorb impact. They are also less expensive than hardshell helmets and are a good choice for climbers on a budget. Both types of helmets are designed to protect the head from impact, penetration, and falling debris. They also have a retention system, which is a strap or harness that keeps the helmet securely on the head.

Hard-shell helmets

Hard-shell helmets have an outer shell made of hard plastic or other materials that offer excellent protection against hard impacts. They are best suited for traditional rock climbing and mountaineering where falling rocks and other debris are common. However, they tend to be heavier than other types of helmets and may be uncomfortable to wear for extended periods.

Foam helmets

Foam helmets are made of expanded polystyrene (EPS) foam and have a softer outer shell than hard-shell helmets. They are lightweight and comfortable to wear, making them a popular choice for sport climbing and other activities where weight is a concern. However, they may not offer as much protection against hard impacts as hard-shell helmets.

Hybrid helmets are a combination of hard-shell and foam helmets, with a hard outer shell and a foam liner. They offer the best of both worlds, with excellent protection against both hard and soft impacts. They are also lightweight and comfortable to wear, making them a popular choice for a wide range of climbing activities.

Overall, the type of climbing helmet you choose will depend on your climbing style, the type of terrain you will be climbing, and your personal preferences. It’s important to choose a helmet that fits well and offers adequate protection for your specific needs.

In addition to the main types of climbing helmets mentioned earlier, there are also some specialized helmets designed for specific climbing activities. Here are some other types of climbing helmets:

Caving helmets

These helmets are specifically designed for caving and spelunking activities. They often have a chinstrap to keep the helmet secure and a built-in headlamp for illumination.

Ice climbing helmets

Ice climbing helmets are similar to rock climbing helmets but are designed to provide additional protection against ice falls and sharp objects like ice axes and crampons.

Ski mountaineering helmets

These helmets are designed for ski mountaineering and backcountry skiing, offering protection against falls, avalanches, and impacts with trees or rocks.

Bicycle helmets

While not specifically designed for climbing, some cyclists use helmets designed for road or mountain biking for climbing activities. These helmets are lightweight, well-ventilated, and often have a visor to protect the face from sun and rain.

Rescue helmets

Rescue helmets are designed for rescue workers and emergency responders who may need to work in hazardous environments, such as collapsed buildings or on high-rise structures.

When choosing a climbing helmet, it’s important to consider the specific needs of your chosen activity to ensure that you have adequate protection. Always make sure that your helmet fits properly and is in good condition before each climb.

How to Choose the Right Climbing Helmet

When choosing a climbing helmet, it is important to consider the following factors:

  • Fit: A helmet should fit snugly on the head without being too tight. It should also not move around when the head is moved.
  • Certification: Look for a helmet that is certified by the Union Internationale des Associations d’Alpinisme (UIAA) or the American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS). These organizations test helmets to ensure they meet safety standards.
  • Ventilation: A helmet with good ventilation will keep the head cool and comfortable while climbing.
  • Weight: A lightweight helmet is easier to wear for long periods of time and is less likely to cause neck strain.
  • Durability: A durable helmet will last longer and provide better protection in the event of an accident.

In addition to these factors, it is also important to consider the type of climbing you will be doing. For example, if you will be climbing in an area with a lot of falling debris, a hardshell helmet may be a better choice. If you will be climbing in a gym, a foam helmet may be a better choice.

Maintenance and Care for Your Climbing Helmet

It is important to maintain and care for your climbing helmet to ensure it continues to provide the best possible protection. Here are some tips for maintaining and caring for your helmet:

  • Clean your helmet regularly with mild soap and water.
  • Inspect your helmet for any signs of wear or damage. If you notice any cracks, dents, or other damage, replace the helmet immediately.
  • Store your helmet in a cool, dry place. Avoid storing it in direct sunlight or in a hot car.
  • Do not drop or hit your helmet. This can cause damage that is not always repairable.

FAQ

How do I know if a climbing helmet fits properly?

A properly fitting climbing helmet should sit level on the head and not be able to rotate around. It should be snug but not tight, and should not move when the head is shaken. It is also important to adjust the straps for a secure fit.

Why is it important to wear a climbing helmet?

A climbing helmet is essential for protecting the head from falling debris and impacts in the event of a fall. It can also offer protection from head injuries caused by hitting the ground or a climbing surface.

What is the best climbing helmet on the market?

The Black Diamond Vector Helmet is considered one of the top climbing helmets on the market due to its combination of comfort, protection, and lightweight design. Other popular options include the Petzl Sirocco and the Mammut Wall Rider.

Are there any safety standards for climbing helmets?

Yes, climbing helmets are required to meet safety standards set by organizations such as UIAA (International Climbing and Mountaineering Federation) and CE (European Committee for Standardization). These standards ensure that the helmet has been tested and meets certain criteria for protection. It is important to check that the helmet you purchase meets these standards.

How often should I replace my climbing helmet?

It is recommended to replace a climbing helmet after any impact, or if it is showing signs of wear and tear. Additionally, it is recommended to replace a climbing helmet every 5 years, as the materials and technology may degrade over time.

Rock climbing is a challenging and exciting sport that requires a great deal of skill, strength, and endurance. It also requires the right climbing gear, including a climbing bag.  In this guide, we'll take a look at some of the best climbing packs for 2023 and what to look for when choosing one. As a climber, when choosing the best rock climbing packs, some of the things to consider includes the size of the backpack for climbing be it best crag packs, best alpine packs

Climbing backpacks come in a variety of sizes, from small daypacks to larger multi-day packs. The size you choose will depend on the type of climbing you’re doing and how much gear you need to carry. Next, consider the features of the backpack. Many climbing backpacks have specialized features such as ice axe loops, rope straps, and crampon pockets. These features can make it easier to carry and organize your gear.

Another important factor to consider is the backpack’s durability. Climbing can be tough on gear, so it’s important to choose a backpack that is made from high-quality materials and is built to withstand the rigors of the sport. Look for backpacks with reinforced seams, durable zippers, and tough fabrics.

One of the best backpacks for 2023 is the Black Diamond Mission pack. This backpack has a capacity of 50 liters, making it perfect for multi-day climbing trips. It also has a variety of specialized features including rope straps, ice axe loops, and crampon pockets. It’s made from durable nylon fabric and has a reinforced design that can withstand the wear and tear of climbing.

Another great option is the Osprey Stratos 24. This pack has a capacity of 24 liters and is perfect for day climbs. It has a variety of pockets and compartments to help you organize your gear and features a ventilated back panel to keep you cool and comfortable on the climb.

Finally, if you’re looking for a backpack that’s designed specifically for climbers, check out the Metolius Bravo II. This backpack has a capacity of 40 liters and is designed with climbers in mind. It has a variety of specialized features including a rope strap and ice axe loops, and is made from durable nylon fabric.

Types of Climbing Backpack

Climbing backpacks, also known as mountaineering backpacks, are specially designed backpacks that are intended for use in climbing and mountaineering expeditions. These backpacks are different from regular backpacks in terms of design, functionality, and durability. Climbing backpacks come in a variety of types, each designed to cater to specific needs and preferences. Here are some of the most common types of climbing backpacks:

READ: Best Climbing Helmet of 2023

Daypacks:

Daypacks are small, lightweight backpacks designed for short day trips. They are usually less than 30 liters in capacity and are ideal for carrying essentials like water, food, and extra clothing layers.

Overnight Backpacks

Overnight backpacks are larger than daypacks and are designed to carry enough gear for an overnight camping trip. They typically range in size from 30 to 50 liters and feature more durable materials, better suspension systems, and additional compartments for gear organization.

Expedition Backpacks

Expedition backpacks are the largest and most heavy-duty backpacks available for mountaineering. They are designed to carry enough gear for multi-day expeditions and feature capacities of 60 liters or more. They also come with advanced suspension systems to distribute weight and offer added support for long treks.

Technical Climbing Backpacks

Technical climbing backpacks are designed for rock and ice climbing expeditions. They are designed to be sleek and streamlined to avoid snagging on rocks and obstacles. They typically feature specialized gear loops, attachment points, and ice axe loops for carrying climbing gear.

Ski Touring Backpacks

Ski touring backpacks are designed for backcountry skiing and snowboarding expeditions. They are typically lightweight and feature slim profiles to allow for freedom of movement during skiing. They come with specialized attachment points for carrying skis or snowboards.

Women’s Backpacks

Women-specific backpacks are designed to accommodate the unique body shapes of female climbers. They feature narrower shoulder straps, shorter torso lengths, and more contoured hip belts for added comfort.

Youth Backpacks

Youth backpacks are designed for young climbers and mountaineers. They typically have smaller capacities, lighter weight, and shorter torso lengths to accommodate smaller body sizes.

FAQ

How do I properly pack a climbing backpack?

When packing a climbing backpack, follow these tips:

  • Pack heavy items at the bottom of the backpack and closer to your back.
  • Use compression straps to keep your gear in place and prevent it from shifting while you're climbing.

  • Use a stuff sack or compression bag to keep your rope tangle-free.
How do I care for my climbing backpack?

  • Clean it with a damp cloth and mild detergent after each use.
  • Air dry the backpack in a well-ventilated area.
  • Store it in a cool, dry place when not in use.
  • Check for any signs of wear or tear and repair or replace any damaged parts.

What should I look for when buying a climbing backpack?

When buying a climbing backpack, consider the following factors:

Climbing slings are an essential piece of climbing gear for any rock climber, providing support and safety while climbing. They come in a variety of materials, sizes, and designs, each with their own unique benefits and drawbacks. In this blog post, we will give you expert advice on the different types of climbing slings available, from contact sling to open loop slings and dynamic slings as well as the pros and cons of each, to help you choose the best sling for your next climbing adventure.

  First, let's take a look at the different types of climbing slings available. There are three main types of slings: webbing slings, dyneema slings, and cordelettes. Webbing slings are made from nylon or polyester and are the most common type of sling used by climbers. They are strong, durable, and easy to handle, making them a great choice for both beginners and experienced climbers. Webbing slings are also relatively inexpensive, which makes them a great option for those on a budget. However, they do have a tendency to stretch over time, which can reduce their strength and safety.

Read: Best Rock Climbers Gear

Dyneema slings, also known as "dyneema runners," are made from a high-strength, low-stretch material that is stronger and more durable than webbing. They are also much thinner and lighter than webbing, making them a great choice for climbers looking to minimize the weight of their gear. However, dyneema slings can be more expensive than webbing and are also more prone to damage from sharp edges and abrasion.

Cordelettes are made from a bundle of nylon or polyester cords and are typically used for building anchors and for equalizing multiple pieces of protection. They are also thicker and more durable than webbing and dyneema slings, and are less prone to stretching. However, they can be difficult to handle and are not recommended for beginners.

When choosing a climbing sling, it's important to consider the type of climbing you'll be doing and the conditions you'll be climbing in. If you're planning on climbing in a gym or on a sport climbing route, webbing slings are a great choice. They are strong, durable, and easy to handle, and are also relatively inexpensive. If you're planning on climbing on a trad or alpine route, dyneema slings are a great choice. They are stronger and more durable than webbing slings, and are also much thinner and lighter, making them a great option for those looking to minimize the weight of their gear.

Finally, if you're planning on building anchors or equalizing multiple pieces of protection, cordelettes are the way to go. They are thicker and more durable than webbing and dyneema slings, and are less prone to stretching. When it comes to the size of the sling, it's important to consider the size of the protection you'll be using. A 60cm sling is a good choice for most climbing routes, and is also the most common size used by climbers. However, if you're planning on climbing on a route with larger protection, a 120cm sling may be a better choice.

In conclusion, climbing slings are an essential piece of equipment for any rock climber, providing support and safety while climbing. They come in a variety of materials, sizes, and designs, each with their own unique benefits and drawbacks. By considering the type of climbing you'll be doing and the conditions you'll be climbing in, as well as the size of the protection you'll be using, you'll be able to choose the best sling for your next climbing adventure.

Types of Slings

Nylon slings

 Made from durable and strong nylon material, these slings are the most common type used in climbing. They come in a variety of lengths and widths to suit different climbing needs.

Dyneema slings

 Made from ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene, Dyneema slings are lighter and stronger than nylon slings. They are more expensive but are popular with sport climbers and alpinists who require lightweight gear.

Spectra slings

 Spectra slings are similar to Dyneema slings, but they are made from a different type of ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene. They are strong and lightweight, making them ideal for alpine climbing and big wall climbing.

Chain slings

 Chain slings are made from metal chains and are used for anchoring and belaying. They are heavier and less flexible than nylon or Dyneema slings but are more durable and suitable for harsh environments.

Sewn slings

 Sewn slings are made from webbing that has been sewn together to form a loop. They are stronger than knotted slings and are commonly used for anchoring, belaying, and rappelling.

Adjustable slings

 Adjustable slings are made from webbing with a buckle or other mechanism that allows the length of the sling to be adjusted. They are useful for setting up anchors or for quickly adjusting the length of a sling during a climb.

Cordelette

 Cordelettes are made from cord and are used for anchoring and building belay stations. They are versatile and can be used in a variety of ways, such as tying a master point or creating a self-equalizing anchor.

Traditional chalk bags are designed for outdoor climbing and are typically made of durable materials such as nylon or canvas. They often have a drawstring closure and a belt loop for easy carrying. Gym chalk bags are designed for indoor climbing and are typically made of a more breathable material such as mesh. They often have a zippered closure and a handle for easy carrying.

FAQ's

How do I choose the right chalk bag for me?

When choosing a chalk bag, consider factors such as shape, size, durability, and additional features. You should also think about how you will be using the bag, such as whether you will be carrying it on your harness or in a backpack.

How do I properly maintain my chalk bag?

To properly maintain your climbing chalk bag, you should clean it regularly with a mild detergent and warm water. You should also be sure to empty the bag of any excess chalk after each use to prevent any build-up of moisture. Make sure to store it in a dry place.

Can I use any type of chalk in my climbing bag?

Most climbing chalk bags are designed to be used with loose chalk, but some may also be compatible with liquid or block chalk. climbing chalk bag is a small, portable bag used to store and dispense chalk, which is used by climbers to dry their hands and improve grip on climbing holds. Climbing chalk bags are essential for any climber, as they allow you to easily access and apply chalk while climbing.

There are several different types of climbing chalk bags, including traditional circular bags, tapered funnel-shaped bags, and bags with built-in pockets or brush holders. Each type of bag has its own advantages and disadvantages, and the best choice will depend on your personal preferences and climbing style.

posts.content:
Las 16 mejores bolsas de tiza en 2023

Las mejores bolsas de tiza para escalada

Es difícil imaginar a un alpinista que se abstenga de usar tiza que ayuda a tener un buen agarre y 'volar' al escalar. Y así es: una bolsa de tiza de alta calidad que sea liviana y fácil de usar solo facilitará el éxito de la escalada de manera rápida y eficiente.

Las mejores marcas de bolsas de tiza para tiza tienen algunas características en común: están construidas con materiales resistentes que no dejan que la tiza se derrame, no son demasiado pesadas para que no interfieran con su viaje y son lo suficientemente anchas para mantener lo que se necesita. contenido.

Desea que su bicicleta mantenga su forma sin sentirse voluminosa cuando la sujeta a su equipo o cinturón. También querrá que la pizarra tenga un diseño sólido ya hecho por una conocida herramienta para exteriores que se esfuerza por especializarse en diseños tradicionales.

Para ayudarlo a encontrar la bolsa de tiza perfecta, hemos elaborado una guía detallada que le permitirá reducir su lista a solo unas pocas opciones. Entre estas excelentes opciones, puede elegir una bolsa de tiza que se ajuste bien a sus medidas.

Las mejores bolsas de tiza en 2026

  • Lienzo Encerado ESTÁTICO
  • Mammut Multipitch
  • Dos Ogros Essential-Z
  • Arc'teryx C80
  • Psicobúlder
  • Juegos Sukoa
  • Cremallera Black Diamond Mojo
  • Diseño de Panda AMC
  • GGBuy Cordón
  • prana

1. Lienzo Encerado ESTÁTICO

Lee la reseña completa
¿Qué le da más confianza a una persona que un producto hecho completamente a mano? Casi nada. La bolsa de tiza encerada de STATIC Climbing es el equipo de escalada original fabricado en el soleado estado de California.

La empresa usó 12 piezas diferentes para coser la bolsa de tiza a mano y creó un producto de color pistola de pólvora que se ve y se siente muy bien.

Está diseñado para durar, independientemente de cuántos paseos hagas en un año: el exterior encerado tiene la culpa (leer = gracias). El cierre Paracord asegura que el contenido de la bolsa de tiza permanezca en su lugar, mientras que el forro polar antibolitas elimina la tiza para brindarle suficientes suministros cuando se le acaba.

El contenido de la bolsa de tiza está mezclado con lavanda natural de San Diego, lo que lo convierte en un accesorio maravilloso.

Especificaciones y características

Material: lona encerada, vellón, correas de polipropileno
Forma: Cilindro
Altura: 7 pulgadas
Altura: 4.5 pulgadas
Ancho: 4.5 pulgadas

2. Mammut Multipitch

No sorprende a los escaladores profesionales que las escaladas de un solo largo y varios largos sean de naturaleza diferente y, por lo tanto, requieran diferentes tipos de equipo. La bolsa de tiza de varios largos

Mammut fue diseñada para aquellos que planean detenerse más de una vez en la estación de seguridad. Es lo suficientemente grande como para almacenar cantidades de tiza más grandes de lo habitual para que las uses cuando llegues a la cima de la roca.

Hay suficiente espacio en los bolsillos incorporados para colocar su protector solar, barra de energía y un teléfono inteligente y usarlo cuando tenga hambre, decida llamar a alguien o se dé cuenta de que es hora de volver a aplicar protector solar. Encontrará un bungee ajustable ubicado en la parte inferior de la bolsa de tiza para sostener su chaqueta cuando hace demasiado calor.

La forma cilíndrica junto con la firme apertura facilita alcanzar el interior de la bolsa de tiza y cerrarla para evitar que se derrame la tiza (el forro polar también ayuda).

Especificaciones y características

Material: nailon.
Forma: Cilíndrica
Altura: 8 pulgadas
Longitud: 7 pulgadas
Ancho: 5 pulgadas

3. Dos Ogros Essential-Z

La bolsa de tiza de escalada de dos Ogros podría ser el artículo más asequible de esta lista, lo que la convierte en una opción atractiva que no arruinará el banco.

Sin embargo, su precio no apunta a su calidad; más bien, esta bolsa de tiza se destaca por su tela duradera de 600 denier y su forro suave que la hace sentir lujosa. El cierre de cordón está construido de manera que evita cualquier derrame de tiza incluso en los momentos en que se cuelga horizontalmente en el suelo.

La bolsa es lo suficientemente grande como para acomodar a los escaladores con manos grandes, lo cual es una buena noticia: la dificultad de encontrar la bolsa de tiza que se ajuste a toda su mano es más que real. La hebilla del cinturón es fina, lo que facilita llevar la bolsa de tiza encima de un arnés.

Encontrará un lugar para guardar su cepillo, un bolsillo con cremallera para mantener su identificación y llaves seguras, y un fondo peludo para la acumulación de polvo de tiza. Si te consideras un principiante, es probable que no encuentres una mejor relación calidad-precio.

Especificaciones y características

Material: Poliéster de 600 denier
Forma: Cilíndrica
Altura: 7 pulgadas
Longitud: 5 pulgadas
Ancho: 5 pulgadas

4. Arc’teryx C80

Leer reseña completa
La bolsa para magnesio Arc'teryx C80 ha sido alabada durante años; seguramente, sus grandes dimensiones junto con la facilidad de uso son impecables.

La circunferencia de 18 pulgadas le permite cargarlo con tiza y esperar que le dure durante largas distancias o escaladas de pared sin excepciones. Este modelo, que presenta un tejido elástico en 4 direcciones de doble tejido Burly que es flexible pero resistente, no te hará pasar minutos tratando de alcanzar la tiza.

El forro polar integrado en la bolsa de tiza hace maravillas para mantener el polvo a raya. El cierre con cordón es de gran calidad, lo que significa que no perderás tiza por el camino. Tiene un bolsillo externo que se adapta bien a las piezas pequeñas que se encuentran cerca de usted, y un cinturón ajustable que ayuda a asegurar el ajuste correcto.

El precio de la bolsa de tiza muerde, a nuestro pesar, pero al menos sabes que estás pagando por el equipo cualitativo que te durará muchos años.

Especificaciones y características

Material: tejido doble corpulento, nailon
Forma: Ligeramente cónico
Altura: 4.7 pulgadas
Longitud: 2 pulgadas
Ancho: 2 pulgadas

5. Psicobúlder

La bolsa de tiza (o, deberíamos decir cubo) de Psychi es un accesorio en un lado más ancho: es un recipiente cónico que puede contener grandes cantidades de tiza y acomodar manos grandes. Puede caber fácilmente en él hasta una libra de tiza y esperar que le dure un día completo de escalada.

Al igual que otras bolsas de tiza, esta tiene un cierre de cordón que facilita el acceso al contenido de la bolsa de tiza y un amplio espacio de almacenamiento para guardar las llaves, los cepillos y un comestible. La bolsa tiene un forro polar que se ocupa de los residuos de tiza y no permite que se derrame en ningún momento durante la escalada.

El color negro lo hace atractivo para aquellos que no están listos para lidiar con la suciedad que aparece después de un par de sesiones de escalada. Si no tiene tiempo para lavar su bolsa de tiza después de cada uso, este modelo de Psychi es su opción.

Especificaciones y características

Material: nailon.
Forma: cónico
Altura: 9 pulgadas
Longitud: 9 pulgadas
Ancho: 8.5 pulgadas

6. Juegos Sukoa

¿Por qué limitarse a equipos que atienden a una sola industria? La bolsa de tiza Sukoa Sports es una prueba de que incluso si un producto se comercializa para escaladores, aún puede usarlo para otras actividades, como CrossFit, gimnasia y levantamiento de pesas.

Cuando agrega una etiqueta de precio muy atractiva, tiene un ganador. Esta bolsa de tiza en forma de cilindro está fabricada con un material resistente al agua que resiste bien incluso con el uso regular.

Es lo suficientemente profundo como para contener grandes cantidades de tiza que te durarán varios días como mínimo sin derrames (gracias al cierre de cordón ajustado y ajustable).

En lugar de un bolsillo con cremallera, obtienes dos, lo que significa que puedes guardar tus objetos de valor como tarjetas de crédito, llaves, identificación y un teléfono inteligente sin preocuparte por perderlos. Además, la bolsa de tiza viene con un cinturón que se puede sujetar cómodamente a su arnés y mosquetones a través de los bucles traseros incorporados.

Especificaciones y características

Material: nailon.
Forma: Cilíndrica
Altura: 7.2 pulgadas
Longitud: 5 pulgadas
Ancho: 5 pulgadas

7. Cremallera Black Diamond Mojo

Los principiantes que aún no han establecido qué características valoran más en una bolsa de tiza de magnesio se beneficiarán al máximo de la bolsa de tiza Mojo de Black Diamond. Este modelo tiene todos los aspectos básicos cubiertos, desde el bolsillo trasero que guarda sus objetos de valor hasta el portaescobillas y un cinturón de cincha incrustado con una hebilla de liberación rápida.

El interior está equipado con un vellón que se siente bien con tiza que se asienta en la parte inferior, mientras que el cierre tiene un diseño de candado con cordón para la seguridad de sus pertenencias.

Hay un bolsillo con cremallera para que guardes tus llaves o una identificación, que siempre es útil. La construcción de la bolsa de tiza le permite mantenerse hacia arriba y no doblarse bajo la influencia de otros objetos. Esto asegura la durabilidad de la bolsa de tiza y la seguridad de las cosas que pones dentro.

Especificaciones y características

Material: poliuretano termoplástico (TPU)
Forma: Cilíndrica
Altura: 14 pulgadas (M/L)
Longitud: 10 pulgadas (M/L)
Ancho: 5 pulgadas (M/L)

8. Diseño de Panda AMC

La bolsa de magnesio para escalada en roca de AMC podría ser el equipo más lindo de esta lista: el estampado de panda definitivamente te hará destacar entre la multitud.

Dicho esto, su funcionalidad no se ve comprometida en absoluto. La bolsa puede contener hasta 0,7 libras de tiza, tiene un cordón fácil de usar y un práctico bolsillo para guardar sus objetos de valor. La amplia abertura significa que los escaladores con manos grandes no tendrán problemas para sumergirse en la bolsa de tiza y sacar la tiza sin derramarla.

Hay un suave forro polar en la parte inferior de la bolsa que acumula los residuos de tiza y le brinda un suministro adicional de tiza cuando la necesita.

Puede sujetar su bolsa de tiza a su arnés con la ayuda de los bucles disponibles o asegurarla alrededor de su cintura; independientemente de cómo lleve su equipo de escalada, nunca se quedará sin tiza.

Especificaciones y características

Material: Poliéster
Forma: Cilíndrica
Longitud: 4,7 pulgadas
Ancho: 5,9 pulgadas

9. GGBuy Cordón

Si tiene poco dinero pero no está dispuesto a conformarse con un equipo de escalada barato, la bolsa de tiza con cordón GGBuy es sin duda su mejor opción. Fabricado con poliéster duradero de 600 denier, está diseñado para durar mucho tiempo sin romperse. Puede sumergir fácilmente su mano en él y así evitar que sus dedos se resbalen cuando está muy por encima del suelo.

El cierre de cordón es de una calidad lo suficientemente alta como para proteger tu tiza y no dejar que se derrame en ningún momento durante la escalada. Los bolsillos delantero y trasero sirven como espacio de almacenamiento para llaves, tarjetas y otros objetos de valor.

La bolsa de tiza viene con un cinturón con hebilla ajustable que se sujeta a la cintura o, en caso de que prefiera tener la tiza colgando del arnés, hay un mosquetón de correa de nailon para utilizar con este propósito.

Especificaciones y características

Material: Poliéster de 600 denier
Forma: Plana
Altura: 7.5 pulgadas
Longitud: 5,1 pulgadas

10. prana

PrAna se enorgullece de la simplicidad y la actitud directa de sus productos, y esto también se refleja en sus bolsas de tiza de magnesio. El material Supersuede de poliéster de la bolsa es agradable al tacto, mientras que el forro polar crea una almohada cómoda para la tiza.

No encontrará características técnicas únicas integradas en la bolsa, pero eso es lo que la hace atractiva. La bolsa tampoco tiene mucha estructura: se mueve cuando escalas pero no interfiere con tu escalada.

Aunque puede que no sea la primera opción de todos los escaladores, puede convertirse fácilmente en una opción para un escalador con un espíritu libre que necesita la cantidad justa de tiza para una sesión de escalada satisfactoria.

Tenga la seguridad de que no lo están engañando con nada: obtiene lo que ve, que es, de hecho, una bolsa de tiza de escalada bien hecha que hace bien su trabajo.

Si solo compruebas una cosa antes de comprar, que sea esta.

Cierre de cordón funcional. El cordón sirve para que la magnesia no acabe en el fondo de la mochila. Debe cerrar de verdad y con una sola mano, y el tope debe sujetar sin apretar demasiado.

Forro polar interior. El forro retiene la magnesia y hace que la mano salga uniformemente cubierta en lugar de con un grumo. Las bolsas de tiza sin forro reparten peor y consumen más magnesia.

Tamaño. Una bolsa pequeña pesa menos y se llena constantemente. Una grande admite la mano completa y molesta al escalar en chimenea. Para uso general, un diámetro que admita la mano abierta hasta la muñeca es el equilibrio correcto.

Cinturón ajustable con hebilla. El cordón con nudo se afloja durante el día. Una hebilla se ajusta con una mano y se quita sin desatar nada, lo que importa cuando llevas arnés.

Bolsillo con cremallera. Para el cepillo, la llave del coche y el móvil. Pequeño detalle, uso constante.

Bolsas de tiza frente a cubos de boulder

Existen dos formatos y sirven para cosas distintas, aunque las tiendas los mezclen.

Bolsas de tiza de cintura. Se llevan puestas mientras escalas, colgadas del cinturón propio o del arnés. Es lo que necesitas para escalada deportiva, tradicional y vías largas.

Cubos de boulder. Más grandes, con base plana y estable, pensados para dejarlos en el suelo. Suelen incluir cepillo y compartimentos, y son lo estándar en bloque porque no escalas con ellos puestos.

Si haces las dos cosas, necesitas los dos formatos. Un cubo no se puede llevar en vía y una bolsa de tiza de cintura es incómoda de compartir en el suelo.

Magnesia en polvo, en bola o líquida. El polvo suelto es el más económico y el que más se dispersa. La bola contiene el polvo y muchos rocódromos la exigen. La magnesia líquida se aplica antes de escalar, deja una base que dura mucho y es la única opción en algunos centros con restricciones de polvo.

Restricciones en interiores. Cada vez más rocódromos limitan la magnesia suelta por calidad del aire. Comprueba la norma antes de comprar bolsas de tiza pensadas para polvo.

Magnesia, restricciones y salud respiratoria

Una parte de la decisión sobre la bolsa de tiza no depende de la bolsa sino de lo que metes dentro, y de dónde escalas.

El polvo en suspensión es un problema real en interiores. La magnesia es carbonato de magnesio, y en un rocódromo con ventilación limitada las partículas finas permanecen en el aire durante horas. Cada vez más centros limitan la magnesia suelta y exigen bola o líquida por este motivo, no por comodidad de limpieza.

Magnesia líquida. Carbonato de magnesio suspendido en alcohol. Se aplica antes de escalar, el alcohol se evapora y deja una capa fina y duradera. No genera polvo, dura mucho más entre aplicaciones y reseca bastante la piel, así que muchos escaladores la usan como base y añaden un poco de polvo encima.

Bola de magnesia. Una malla rellena de polvo que dosifica al apretarla. Es el compromiso habitual: menos dispersión que el polvo suelto y sin la sequedad de la líquida.

Si tienes la piel sensible o problemas respiratorios, la líquida es la opción más razonable, y conviene lavarse las manos al terminar. La orientación general sobre exposición a polvo respirable en espacios cerrados está recogida por organismos de salud laboral como la Health and Safety Executive británica, y aunque la magnesia no es un polvo especialmente peligroso, los principios de ventilación y reducción de la exposición se aplican igual en un rocódromo.

Comprueba la norma antes de comprar. No tiene sentido elegir una bolsa de tiza optimizada para polvo suelto si tu centro habitual solo permite bola o líquida.

Cuidado de tu bolsa de tiza

Vacíalas al final de la temporada. La magnesia acumulada apelmaza el forro y reduce su capacidad de retención.

Lávalas a mano y en frío. Sin detergente fuerte, que deja residuo. Sécalas del revés y a la sombra.

Cepilla el forro periódicamente. Un forro polar apelmazado deja de repartir bien la magnesia y da la impresión de que la bolsa es mala cuando solo está sucia.

Guárdalas cerradas. Es para lo que sirve el cordón. Una bolsa abierta en la mochila cubre de blanco todo lo demás.

Sustituye el cordón cuando se deshilache. Cuesta céntimos y es la reparación que alarga más la vida útil de las bolsas de tiza.

No la metas en la lavadora. El aro rígido se deforma y la bolsa pierde precisamente la propiedad por la que la compraste.

Conclusión: cómo elegir tu bolsa de tiza

Elige tu bolsa de tiza por tres cosas: que la apertura se mantenga abierta, que el cordón cierre de verdad y que el interior tenga forro polar. El estampado, la marca y el precio importan bastante menos de lo que sugiere el escaparate.

Si estás completando el equipo, nuestras guías sobre mosquetones, paquetes de escalada y cascos cubren el resto de lo esencial.

posts.title: Cómo elegir eslingas, cuerdas y correas para escalar
posts.excerpt: Cuando estás en el extremo afilado de la cuerda, un portaequipajes bien abastecido es tan importante como un asegurador de confianza. Si te estás iniciando en la escalada tradicional, necesitarás…
posts.content:
Cómo elegir eslingas de escalada, cinta y cordino

Cuando estás en el extremo afilado de la cuerda, un portaequipajes bien abastecido es tan importante como un asegurador de confianza. Si te estás iniciando en la escalada tradicional, necesitarás saber cómo elegir y usar lo siguiente:

  • Eslingas (también conocidas como corredores)
  • Cincha
  • Cable

Estos artículos son adaptables a una serie de usos y actúan como herramientas múltiples en su arsenal de escalada.

Si estás buscando información sobre cintas exprés, consulta nuestros artículos detallados sobre cómo elegirlas y cómo usarlas.

Eslingas de escalada

eslingas de escalada en mosquetones utilizadas como cintas exprés

Aunque se puede hacer de varias maneras, un cabestrillo (también conocido como corredor) generalmente se crea cosiendo una sección de cincha en un bucle. Una eslinga se puede usar como una cinta exprés extendida para permitir que la cuerda corra más recta y disminuir la fricción en las rutas errantes, o se puede usar para colocar un ancla.

Longitud de la eslinga

Las eslingas de escalada vienen en una variedad de longitudes, anchos y pesos. Las eslingas de escalada más largas son más efectivas para reducir el arrastre de la cuerda que una cinta exprés, pero también son más pesadas y voluminosas.

Las eslingas de escalada de una sola longitud (60 cm/24 pulg.) son una longitud útil, aproximadamente 2 o 3 veces más largas que la mayoría de las cintas exprés; tienen una buena longitud para usar sobre un hombro o como una cinta exprés alpina.

Las eslingas de escalada de doble longitud (120 cm/48 pulg.) le brindan una mayor extensión para reducir el arrastre de la cuerda o el posicionamiento profesional; un tamaño perfecto para construir anclajes fijos de dos pernos, se pueden usar doblados sobre un hombro o como una cinta exprés alpina.

Las eslingas de escalada extralargas (180–240 cm/72–96 pulg.) son buenas para enrollar rocas grandes y conectar tres puntos de protección para hacer un ancla.

Los slings más cortos (30 cm/12 pulgadas y más cortos) son de un tamaño intermedio que no se usaría con frecuencia; algunos escaladores los usan para atar pitones.
Los arneses Quickdraw son arneses precosidos que le permiten hacer sus propios 'sorteos' agregando los mosquetones que elija.

Materiales de la eslinga

Durante años, el material principal de los arneses de escalada ha sido el nailon. También se ha utilizado poliéster, pero no es tan común como el nailon. En los últimos años, los polietilenos de ultra alto peso molecular (UHMW), con marcas como Dyneema, Dynex y Spectra, han ganado popularidad. Algunas correas se fabrican mezclando nailon con uno de estos materiales de marca superresistentes.

El material de una eslinga de escalada afecta el peso, la resistencia, la longevidad, el uso potencial y el precio de un artículo:

Ventajas del nailon:

Más asequible
Sostiene mejor los nudos y los nudos son más fuertes, debido a su elasticidad y textura.
El estiramiento y la temperatura de fusión más alta lo ayudan a manejar las fuerzas dinámicas (caídas)
Ventajas de los polietilenos UHMW de marca (Dyneema, Dynex y Spectra):

Ultraligero, debido a una relación resistencia-peso ultra alta
Más resistente a los rayos UV
No se congelará cuando se moje
Siempre que tenga mucho cuidado al atar los nudos y evite cualquier escenario en el que una carga de caída no esté soportada por una cuerda dinámica, Spectra, Dyneema y Dynex se pueden usar para la mayoría de las aplicaciones de escalada.

Cinta de escalada

correas de escalada atadas a un cabestrillo usando un nudo de agua

La mayoría de los escaladores tradicionales llevan secciones adicionales de correas para crear eslingas de longitud personalizada para extender o construir un ancla. Las correas a granel se venden por pie, en carretes o en secciones.

Tipos de correas
Hay dos tipos de correas:

Las correas tubulares son el estándar para escalar. La geometría tubular de la correa trepadora la hace más resistente y duradera que una correa plana de ancho similar. También es más flexible, por lo que los nudos atados con él son más fáciles de crear y más fuertes.
Las correas planas generalmente se usan para reemplazar las correas de las mochilas, construir sus propios estriberes o amarrar el equipo.

Anchos de cincha
Los anchos disponibles para correas tubulares a granel incluyen 1” y 5/8”. Una pulgada es el ancho estándar para hacer anclas, mientras que 5/8” se usa a menudo para hacer eslingas caseras. (Las correas planas vienen en una variedad de anchos, los más comunes son de 2" y 1").

Especificaciones de las correas
Las correas tubulares a granel están disponibles en "especificaciones para escalada" y "especificaciones militares". La especificación de escalada es más gruesa, más pesada y más resbaladiza, mientras que la especificación militar es más delgada, más liviana y tiene una textura superficial más rugosa. Ambos son muy duraderos, pero las correas con especificaciones de escalada son un poco más fuertes y más fáciles de atar, y sujetan los nudos de manera más segura. (REI generalmente solo lleva correas tubulares con especificaciones de escalada).

Material de las correas
Las correas a granel solo están disponibles en nailon. Si fabrica sus propias eslingas, ate la correa de nailon con un nudo de agua que tenga colas largas (de al menos 2 pulgadas de largo).

Compre correas a granel

cuerda de escalada
cuerda de escalada unida a mosquetones

El cordón es útil para crear eslingas de longitud personalizada, como una cordelette, que se puede usar en la construcción de anclajes o en enganches de fricción para rápeles y escalada artificial. El cable viene en diámetros desde 1 mm hasta 9 mm, a veces mayor. Se vende por pie o en secciones: las secciones de 20 o 30 pies son longitudes comunes.

Materiales del cordón
Al igual que las eslingas de escalada, el cable está disponible en dos materiales diferentes: perlón (un tipo de nailon) y polietileno UHMW (como Dyneema o Spectra).

El material afecta el peso, la resistencia, la longevidad, el uso potencial y el precio.
